test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 14 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Why is infrastructure referred to as a 'universal intermediate'?

options.text: It is the most profitable sector.
It is universally available in every country.
It is used in the production of nearly all goods and services.
It connects urban and rural areas.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It is used in the production of nearly all goods and services**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Infrastructure** is commonly referred to as a **'universal intermediate'** because it forms the backbone of economic activities and is essential for the production of goods and services.
 
• It includes facilities and services like **transportation, communication, power supply, water, sanitation, and social infrastructure**, which are fundamental for the functioning of any economy.
 
• The term **'universal intermediate'** signifies that infrastructure is a prerequisite for almost every sector, including agriculture, industry, and services, to function efficiently.
 
• Without proper infrastructure, the production and distribution of goods and services become inefficient, leading to higher costs and reduced economic growth.
 
• Infrastructure supports economic development by improving connectivity, increasing productivity, and fostering trade and commerce across different regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Importance of Infrastructure:**

 
 
• **Economic Growth:** Infrastructure development is a key driver of economic growth as it enhances productivity and creates jobs.
 
• **Global Competitiveness:** Countries with robust infrastructure attract more investments, fostering overall economic development.
 
• **Social Benefits:** Infrastructure development improves access to basic amenities such as education, healthcare, and sanitation, enhancing the quality of life.
 
• **Environmental Impact:** Sustainable infrastructure reduces environmental degradation through the use of renewable energy sources and eco-friendly construction practices.
 
 
 
• **Types of Infrastructure:**
 
 
• **Physical Infrastructure:** Includes tangible facilities such as roads, bridges, railways, airports, and power plants.
 
• **Social Infrastructure:** Comprises healthcare, education, housing, and sanitation facilities that improve living standards.
 
• **Digital Infrastructure:** Refers to IT and communication networks, including the internet, broadband, and data centers.
 
 
 
• **Role of Infrastructure in Sustainable Development:**
 
 
• Infrastructure projects like renewable energy plants (solar, wind) contribute to **sustainable energy solutions**.
 
• Efficient public transportation systems reduce **carbon emissions** and promote environmental sustainability.
 
• Smart city initiatives integrate technology with urban planning to enhance the quality of urban life.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Infrastructure Projects:**
 
 
• The **Golden Quadrilateral Project** in India connects major cities through a network of highways, boosting trade and transportation.
 
• The **BharatNet Project** aims to provide high-speed internet connectivity to rural areas.
 
• Development of metro systems in cities like Delhi and Mumbai to enhance urban mobility.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Infrastructure Index:**

 
 
• The **Global Infrastructure Hub** monitors global infrastructure development trends and highlights areas needing improvement.
 
• India ranks among the top countries investing in infrastructure development, with significant projects like the **Smart Cities Mission** and **Bharatmala Project**.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Infrastructure Development:**
 
 
• **Funding Constraints:** Many developing countries face a lack of financial resources for large-scale infrastructure projects.
 
• **Land Acquisition Issues:** Land acquisition for infrastructure often faces delays due to disputes and resistance from local communities.
 
• **Environmental Concerns:** Large-scale projects may lead to deforestation, displacement of communities, and environmental degradation.
